fixes.explanation: The text says Moses goes over to look at the bush. It doesn't say anything about what he does with the flock. He thinks, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?” (Exodus 3:3) That's a man walking toward the fire, not away from it. I'd have a hard time walking away from a bush that's on fire and won't burn up.

Holy is right. God says, “Do not come any closer… Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.” (Exodus 3:5) Moses is out in the wilderness at the mountain of God, and God is calling to him from the bush. The ground gets called holy, and God tells him to take his sandals off.

Not quite. The text says, “At this, Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.” (Exodus 3:6) God had just named Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I think that's the moment my own face would have disappeared behind my mustache.

True. God tells Moses, “The elders of Israel will listen to what you say…” (Exodus 3:18) Moses hasn't said a word to them yet, and God is already telling him how that part goes. I'd love that before a big meeting at work: the room is already listening.

That's not what God says. His words are that the king “…will not allow you to go unless a mighty hand compels him.” (Exodus 3:19) God puts the mighty hand first. Then He says, “And after that, he will release you.” (Exodus 3:20)

That's right. God says every woman will ask “…her neighbor and any woman staying in her house for silver and gold jewelry and clothing…” (Exodus 3:22) Just before that, He says, “…you will not go away empty-handed.” (Exodus 3:21) I like that God gets specific. He doesn't just say it'll be fine, He names the jewelry and the clothing.

No glowing hands here, friend. The text says, “…when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.” (Exodus 4:6) Nothing in the verse shines. A glowing hand would be handy for finding the cookie jar at midnight, but that's my kitchen, not Exodus.

Finest speaker in Egypt would be quite the upgrade, but that's a bigger promise than the one the LORD makes. He says, “I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.” (Exodus 4:12) Moses still does the speaking, with help and teaching. Honestly, I'd take that deal. The only thing anybody ever taught me was how to press a stamp straight.
Moses doesn't ask to wait. He says, “Please, Lord, send someone else.” (Exodus 4:13) I've hit the snooze button plenty of times, but this is more like asking a coworker to take your shift.

Caleb shows up later, as one of the men Moses sends to scout Canaan (Numbers 13:6). The LORD names Aaron the Levite here, Moses' brother. (Exodus 4:14) Caleb is a fine name to have in mind, friend, just a different man.

Not quite. The LORD says of Aaron, “When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.” (Exodus 4:14) The LORD also says Aaron is on his way to meet Moses. I think a glad face coming down the road is a good start for a trip like this.
